subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get their own `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or stay with per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This chooses a new security-sensitive config/default behavior and precedence across existing policy layers, which repository policy treats as a maintainer product/security decision rather than a routine bug fix.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` as the explicit operator-wide layer and document how it composes with per-job `payload.toolsAllow` and delivery modes.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron isolated runs as subagent-like for tool policy, reducing new config surface but making `tools.subagents.tools` affect cron jobs too.

options.title: Keep per-job controls only
options.body: Avoid adding global config and instead improve delivery safeguards and docs around `payload.toolsAllow` for each cron job.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` as the explicit operator-wide layer and document how it composes with per-job `payload.toolsAllow` and delivery modes.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review and central cron/config discussion make steipete the best current routing candidate for the product/security precedence choice.
